messages.author: caaac2dc0aae28b8
messages.subject: Re: occuFP
parts:
Dave;

Thanks for getting to this so quickly. I tried your suggestion with my own data and found it worked similarly. Specifically, I first got a "reversed" solution using method="Nelder-Mead", which I then used to give occuFP the "correct" starting values, and thus obtained the sensible solution. I'm glad you incorporated this function into unmarked.

Eric


On Friday, October 19, 2012 4:25:35 PM UTC-4, David Miller wrote:
Hi Eric -
 
Thanks for putting the new function to the test. When I tested the function I only used examples with more than one of the data types. I will see if I can come up with a more permanent fix but here is what seems to be going on and a solution that seems to work and gets me the right answers.
 
So I am not exactly sure why the starting values of all 0s is a problem but in fitting the false positive models, starting values seem to be more important than with other occupancy models. Switching the method to 'Nelder-Mead' seems to work better. I tried that and got:
 
> m1.bird <- occuFP(detformula = ~ 1, FPformula = ~1, stateformula = ~ 1, data = bird.umf, method = "Nelder-Mead")
> m1.bird

Call:
occuFP(detformula = ~1, FPformula = ~1, stateformula = ~1, data = bird.umf, 
    method = "Nelder-Mead")

Occupancy:
 Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
   -0.818 0.751 -1.09   0.276

Detection:
 Estimate   SE     z P(>|z|)
    -4.96 4.68 -1.06   0.288

false positive:
 Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
    -1.36 0.216 -6.29 3.1e-10

AIC: 445.1639
 
 
This is a correct answer, but as Royle and Link point out - the likelihood is identical if you switch the true positive and false positive detection probabilities and substitute psi with 1-psi. This is what happened here where the estimated psi is 0.306. I will work and see if I can get something to catch this automatically but having a false positive probability than true positive probability is a red flag. For now I found that choosing the right starting values avoids this. If you start with the true positive detection being very high and the false positive very low, the optimizing algorithm will head to the answer you want. For example:
 
 
> m1.bird <- occuFP(detformula = ~ 1, FPformula = ~1, stateformula = ~ 1, data = bird.umf, starts = c(2,2,-3))
> m1.bird

Call:
occuFP(detformula = ~1, FPformula = ~1, stateformula = ~1, data = bird.umf, 
    starts = c(2, 2, -3))

Occupancy:
 Estimate    SE    z P(>|z|)
     0.82 0.749 1.09   0.274

Detection:
 Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
    -1.36 0.216 -6.31 2.81e-10

false positive:
 Estimate   SE     z P(>|z|)
    -4.97 4.69 -1.06   0.289

AIC: 445.1639 
> backTransform(m1.bird, type = 'state') 
Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Occupancy estimate(s)

 Estimate    SE LinComb (Intercept)
    0.694 0.159    0.82           1

Transformation: logistic
 
 
I hope this is helpful and will try to work on making the function more stable when only type 2 data is used.
 
Dave

messages.author: 72543510936c4f8a
messages.subject: Re: occuFP
parts:
I'm running occupancy on an interview survey dataset from 69 cells with max. 7 respondents. To account for false positive responses among the others, I'm using occuFP. 

However, running my null model, it appears that there is a problem with the optimizing algorithm:

Mod.Null <- occuFP(detformula = ~ 1, FPformula = ~ 1, stateformula = ~ 1, data = occUMF)
backTransform(Mod.Null, type="state")

Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Occupancy estimate(s)

 Estimate      SE LinComb (Intercept)

0.5 1432316       0           1

Transformation: logistic 

Following the discussion here, when I use "Nelder-Mead" as the method, things appear work but I'm still unsure: 

Mod.Null <- occuFP(detformula = ~ 1, FPformula = ~ 1, stateformula = ~ 1, data = occUMF, method = "Nelder-Mead")
backTransform(Mod.Null, type="state")

Backtransformed linear combination(s) of Occupancy estimate(s)

 Estimate    SE LinComb (Intercept)

0.579 0.268   0.317           1

Transformation: logistic 

I appreciate it if anyone could help me understand why this problem is occurring and how should I define the starting values?
